statements.text: The Remote Access Security Act is a critical step aimed at addressing a loophole that currently exists in U.S. export control laws that allows bad actors, like the CCP, to access U.S. technology through cloud technology.
statements.context: Remarks delivered during a House Foreign Affairs Committee markup of various measures.

statements.text: Chinese companies have been remotely accessing tech covered by export controls, enabling the CCP to continue using U.S. chips to develop AI and modernize their military forces.
statements.context: House floor speech by Rep. Mike Lawler urging passage of the Remote Access Security Act.

statements.text: Today, as technology has developed rapidly in the last few years, many sensitive technologies can be accessed remotely through cloud services. [...] As a result, companies aligned with the Chinese Communist Party have been exploiting remote access loopholes and are using American technology to advance their AI development, military capabilities, and potentially much worse.
statements.context: House committee markup of the Remote Access Security Act, a bill to extend export controls to cloud-based technologies.

statements.text: Export controls exist to limit critical technology developed in the U.S. from falling into the hands of our adversaries. Export controls are a major tool of the administration to protect sensitive tech and bolster our own national security, and these rules have never been more timely or important as China seeks to enhance their chip and AI development. Unfortunately, there is a major loophole in our export control regime. As the laws and regulations are written, physical export controls do not apply to remote access of items. This means that still to this day, the CCP can access our tech through the cloud and utilize it for their own malicious purposes. Our export controls are only as strong as the weakest link, and right now, the CCP has a real tool to sidestep these prohibitions. We need action now.
statements.context: Floor speech in the U.S. House of Representatives advocating for the Remote Access Security Act, which would extend export controls to cloud-based remote access of controlled technology.
